preamble: Voicing of the voiceless uvular stop [q] to [ɢ]. In central and northwestern Iranian Persian (including Tehrani), the letter ق, which stood for Arabic [q] in Early New Persian, merged with غ [ɣ] into one phoneme realized as a voiced uvular stop [ɢ] except in unstressed intervocalic position, where it is a fricative.

examples.from: Early New Persian ق [q] (in Arabic loans such as قلب qalb 'heart')
examples.note: The voiced stop [ɢ] is the default realization; unstressed intervocalic tokens are [ɣ~ʁ]. Many other Iranian dialects keep q and ɣ apart.
